This is the first compliance hire for our North American businesses: a Canadian and a US money services business in a regulated payments group. You will hold three roles at both entities: Compliance Officer, Risk Officer, and Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO). The job is to build the programs, then run them.
 
Both businesses are early. They move money across borders for business clients, with foreign exchange where needed, and their volumes are starting now. You will work with a small team and can bring in outside providers for monitoring and reviews, working under your direction. You will report to David.


As Compliance Officer (both entities)
• Build, then keep current, each entity's written compliance program, with policies approved by a senior officer: client and beneficial-ownership due diligence, enhanced measures for higher-risk clients, record keeping, travel-rule data and training.

• Assess money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions-evasion risk across clients, products, delivery channels and geographies, and assess new products, payment rails and corridors before launch.

• Set the outside compliance provider's scope, review its work and sign off what it produces.

• Run the written, ongoing training program and its training plan for staff and anyone acting for the entities.

• Keep each entity's registrations current: the money services business registration with FINTRAC and the payment service provider registration with the Bank of Canada in Canada; the FinCEN registration in the US, renewed every two years and re-filed within 180 days of a triggering change.

• Lead regulator examinations and requests for information, and answer due-diligence requests from banks, payout partners and clients.

• Monitor state money transmission licensing requirements for the US entity's activity, and advise the business before it enters a new state or product.

As MLRO (both entities)
• Run transaction monitoring and sanctions screening, and decide every escalated alert.

• Canada: file suspicious transaction reports with FINTRAC as soon as practicable after reasonable grounds to suspect are established, and terrorist property reports; oversee the prescribed reports, including international electronic funds transfers and virtual currency receipts of C$10,000 or more.

• US: file suspicious activity reports with FinCEN for suspicious transactions of US$2,000 or more within 30 days of initial detection, and keep them with their supporting documents for five years; oversee currency transaction reporting and OFAC blocking and reject reporting.

• Act as the contact for law enforcement requests and production orders, and protect the confidentiality of every report.

As Risk Officer (both entities)
• Canada: act as the senior officer who oversees the written risk management and incident response framework under the Retail Payment Activities Regulations, its incident reports and its third-party risk, and any safeguarding-of-funds framework if end-user funds are held.

• Canada: file the annual report to the Bank of Canada by March 31, and give notice of a significant change or new activity at least five business days before it happens.

• Maintain each entity's risk register and risk appetite, covering compliance, operational, third-party and partner risk, and report it to the board.

• Commission the independent reviews: FINTRAC's effectiveness review at least every two years, the Bank of Canada framework review at least every three years, and the US program's independent review; track every finding to closure.

Must have
• At least 7 years in anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance at money services businesses, payment companies or the payments arm of a bank, including 3 or more as a compliance officer, MLRO or deputy.

• Deep knowledge of Canada's Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC's guidance, and working knowledge of the Retail Payment Activities Act.

• Has built a compliance program, not only run one: written its policies, risk assessment and training plan.

• Has decided on and filed suspicious transaction reports, and has run transaction monitoring and sanctions screening.

• Has taken a business through a FINTRAC, bank-partner or audit examination and closed the findings.

• Due diligence on business clients, including clients that pay out for their own customers, and on banks and payout partners.

• A recognised AML certification, such as CAMS, or equivalent experience.

• Writes clearly for boards, regulators and banks, and works alone across time zones.

About the Opportunity

This is an exciting opportunity to lead the Financial Crime QA team within the Compliance Assurance function of a regulated crypto business. As QA Team Lead, you will manage a team of QA Analysts who review AML Transaction Monitoring alerts, Name Screening, EDD and other financial crime investigations.

You will own the day-to-day delivery and quality of the QA program, set and uphold review standards, and develop your team's expertise. QA Program Ownership – Own the end-to-end delivery of QA reviews across Transaction Monitoring, Name Screening, Sanctions, EDD and other AML investigations. Ensure reviews are completed on time, to a consistent standard, and in line with agreed sampling plans and service levels.

Management Information & Reporting – Produce and present QA MI, dashboards and trend analysis to Financial Crime and Compliance leadership. Identify systemic issues, root causes and emerging risks, and translate findings into clear, actionable recommendations for management and governance forums.

•

Stakeholder Management – Act as the primary QA point of contact for Financial Crime Operations leadership, Team Leads, Product, Policy and other Compliance teams. Coaching & Quality Improvement – Partner with Operations and Training teams to turn QA findings into targeted coaching, training content and procedural updates. Act as a Subject Matter Expert on AML investigations, crypto typologies and regulatory expectations.

You will own the trade operating model, the end-to-end order and settlement flow, cash flows, corporate actions, reconciliations, and regulatory readiness across the business.

 - Own the end-to-end order flow for US equities, from inception through clearing and settlement, including reconciliation, corporate actions, and exception management

 - Serve as a named principal of Kraken Securities LLC and act as an operational control point — including dual-approval (“four eyes”) sign-off on transactions and asset movements, with coverage across time zones

 - Design and implement the operating model for Kraken Securities and xStocks, aligned to strategic goals

 - Build and run the operating systems for the business — policies, written supervisory procedures, controls, books and records, business continuity, and KPIs — and translate C-suite goals into clear targets for each business unit

 - Set performance targets, monitor progress, and report KPIs and costs transparently to leadership

 - Hire and develop a high-performing operations team, build the licensing bench and succession plan, and build the organizational structure to scale

 - Partner with functional leaders across Marketing, Compliance, Product, Engineering, and Operations to keep initiatives aligned and moving

 - Contribute to strategy and growth planning to help build a sustainable business

 - Support functions such as HR and IT in building procedures that link to corporate strategy

 - Experience in crypto, brokerage, advisory, fintech, or another highly regulated industry

 - In-depth knowledge of traditional financial markets — execution, clearing, settlement, custody, margin, securities lending, and corporate actions

 - Working understanding of digital assets and tokenized securities, including custody models, on-chain settlement, and the operational controls they demand

 - Direct experience operating under SEC and FINRA rules — books and records, supervisory procedures, trade reporting, and examination response

 - A proven record of defining structured approaches to solve complex challenges

The ML & Discovery team in Consumer Growth builds the machine learning systems that help millions of customers discover what to trade and engage with next across crypto, equities, derivatives, and prediction markets. Our models and platforms power personalized feed and asset ranking, intelligent notification orchestration, and LLM-driven market insights across the Coinbase app. As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer (L5) you will own end-to-end initiatives across the ML lifecycle, from problem formulation, feature engineering, and modeling to production serving and online A/B experimentation. Partnering closely with Product, Data Science, and Engineering in a high-velocity, data-driven environment, you will shape our team's roadmap, raise our engineering quality bar, and use AI-native workflows to deliver measurable business impact.

What you’ll do:

• Own end-to-end machine learning initiatives from problem formulation and offline evaluation to production deployment and online A/B testing, driving measurable lifts in user engagement, retention, and trading activity.

• Design intelligent notification orchestration, candidate ranking, and targeting systems that match users with timely, high-value alerts while avoiding fatigue and improving user experience.

• Develop production LLM pipelines, grounding workflows, and automated evaluation loops that generate accurate, real-time market insights and personalized financial content.

• Architect resilient, low-latency model serving services and real-time feature pipelines, eliminating technical debt, leading incident response, and raising our operational reliability bar.

• Partner with Product, Data Science, and Engineering to shape the team roadmap, mentor L3-L4 engineers, and build AI-native workflows and automation that multiply team velocity.

Required Skills and Experience:

• 5+ years of experience in machine learning engineering and software development, with a track record of shipping production ML systems that move customer and business metrics.

• Proven track record in one or more relevant domains: recommendation systems, multi-stage ranking and retrieval, contextual bandits, notification targeting, or production LLM applications.

• Strong software engineering and data skills in a backend language like Python or Go, with hands-on proficiency in modern ML and data stacks (such as PyTorch, GBDTs, Spark/Databricks, Ray, Kafka, and/or Tecton).

• Deep practical knowledge of offline model evaluation, training-serving skew mitigation, and design/interpretation of online A/B experiments tied to business metrics.

• Demonstrated ability to drive complex projects end-to-end, make pragmatic architectural trade-offs, and mentor junior engineers.

• Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

When crypto moves between exchanges, regulators in most major markets require that customer information travels with the transaction — the same idea as a bank wire. That's the Travel Rule, and Coinbase built TRUST (Travel Rule Universal Solution Technology), the industry's leading Travel Rule network with 200+ member VASPs. As PM, you'll own the platform behind it and the consumer experience in front of it, and you'll grow TRUST as a global standard.

What you'll do:

• Drive TRUST network growth: sign new VASPs, expand asset and network support, and lead go-to-market to strengthen TRUST's position globally

• Own the end-to-end Travel Rule experience, from the platform APIs and backend infrastructure to the consumer flows that make compliance feel effortless

• Shape consumer experiences that make cross-exchange transfers feel easy, transparent, and trustworthy, even while regulatory data exchange happens behind the scenes

• Partner across product groups so teams that own their own front-end surfaces integrate cleanly with Travel Rule infrastructure

• Support global expansion by enabling new Coinbase entities and meeting jurisdiction-specific requirements across markets like the EU, UK, and India

• Strengthen TRUST's privacy and security posture to reinforce Coinbase's position as the most trusted platform in crypto

• Lead program health and stakeholder alignment across a complex, multi-team domain where you are the single-threaded owner

• 7+ years of product management experience

• Business development and partnership mindset: you understand how to build a business, grow adoption, and form relationships that expand a platform's reach

• Experience building platform or API products that other teams integrate with

• Strong consumer product instincts, with care for an easy-to-use, trustworthy customer experience

• Experience with compliance, regulatory, or risk products in fintech or financial services

• Strong analytical skills, with experience defining success metrics across both platform health and user experience

Role Overview
We are seeking a senior trust, custody, and treasury professional to serve as Chief Trust Officer and Treasurer for an OCC-chartered trust bank and a state-chartered trust bank. This role combines responsibility for the safety and control of client assets with oversight of the bank’s treasury operations, balance sheet, capital, and liquidity.
The successful candidate will bring deep experience in digital-asset custody and treasury operations, sound judgment in regulated environments, and the ability to operate effectively in a growing, cross-functional organization.


Key Responsibilities
• Serve as Trust Officer and Treasurer, subject to applicable regulatory approval and required vetting.

• Oversee fund movements, ensuring appropriate controls, documentation, and approvals.

• Oversee account reconciliations and help ensure client assets are safeguarded, accurately recorded, and supported by strong financial controls.

• Oversee bank accounts and treasury operations, including management of the balance sheet and capital and liquidity buffers.

• Partner with Legal, Compliance, Finance, Operations, Product, and senior leadership on regulatory expectations, controls, and operating readiness.

• Support the design, implementation, and ongoing improvement of custody, treasury, reconciliation, and financial-control processes.

• Prepare for and support financial-statement, custody, SOC, and other applicable audits and regulatory reviews.

Required Qualifications
• At least 10 years of relevant professional experience in digital-asset custody, treasury operations, banking, trust, or closely related fields.

• Demonstrated experience with digital-asset custody and treasury operations; experience at a crypto custodian, regulated trust company, or bank is strongly valued.

• Experience working with the OCC or a state banking regulator, or directly supporting a regulated trust or banking organization through regulatory requirements.

• Strong understanding of bank accounts, balance-sheet management, capital, liquidity, reconciliations, and financial controls.

• Ability to be based in Chicago and work from the Chicago office as needed in a hybrid environment.

• Ability to pass required government background checks relating to financial condition and character.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience working for or with a digital-asset custodian.

• Experience with custody of traditional assets, combined with a demonstrated willingness and ability to develop deep expertise in crypto custody.

• Experience supporting financial-statement audits, custody audits, SOC audits, or similar control assessments.

• Experience in a regulated trust company or bank, even if the experience is outside digital assets.

• Experience operating in a lean, high-growth environment where the role requires practical judgment, ownership, and close cross-functional collaboration.

The role reports locally to the Senior Reporting Manager, based in London, within the Group Reporting team.

Your role in the Team's Success:
The Group Reporting Manager plays a key role in ensuring the accuracy and completeness of IG’s internal and external financial reporting. You will take ownership of the Group’s month-end consolidation and close, manage the interim and year-end reporting processes, and review the work of the wider reporting team ahead of key deadlines.
You will liaise with, and support, all areas of the business that impact the Group’s financial position.

• Review the work of the wider Group Reporting team — including submissions from Financial Control (Kraków) and colleagues in London — ahead of year-end and throughout the reporting cycle.
• Manage the Group’s interim (half-year) and year-end reporting processes, including the preparation and review of the Group’s financial statements.
• Support metadata changes within the consolidation tool and the maintenance of the Group’s chart of accounts, acting as backup to the primary owner.
• Lead key internal stakeholder management, partnering with the wider business — across an international stakeholder base including Financial Control (Kraków) and regional controllers — on Group financial reporting matters.
• Prepare the monthly Financial Management Information (FMI) pack, including commentary on the key drivers of performance and position.
• Prepare the Group’s monthly cash flow analysis, identifying and explaining the key movements and drivers.
• Drive continuous improvement in Group financial processes, working closely with the Finance Systems team, Financial Control (Kraków) and regional controllers to implement operational changes.
• Act as financial controller of certain intermediate holding companies, owning their month-end close, statutory reporting and controls.
• Act as a key point of contact for external auditors.
• Support across a wider range of Group Reporting activities and projects as the team’s remit evolves.

• ACA/ACCA or local equivalent professional accounting qualification, with strong post-qualification experience (typically around 4+ years’ PQE).
• Audit experience, ideally Big 4 trained.
• Strong multi-currency consolidation experience, including the translation and consolidation of foreign operations.
• Demonstrable experience owning or running a Group month-end close and consolidation end-to-end — rather than partial or single-entity sub-consolidation.
• Experience of managing interim (half-year) and year-end reporting processes and financial statements.
• Hands-on, in-house Group consolidation and reporting experience under IFRS.
• Experience with a Group consolidation system (HFM, or a direct equivalent such as OneStream or Oracle FCCS).
• Strong stakeholder management skills across a diverse, international range of internal stakeholders, with the ability to influence and drive outcomes.
• Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to dive into the detail.
• Confidence to challenge current ways of working and thrive in a dynamic environment subject to regulatory and commercial change.

Desirable

About the role –

As a Senior IAM Engineer, you will be a key member of the Enterprise IT organization, serving as a senior hands-on engineer responsible for the design, implementation, and operation of our enterprise-wide Identity and Access Management program.

The role will be responsible for engineering and delivering IAM solutions across Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), Identity Providers (IdP/SSO), Privileged Access Management (PAM), and directory services. You will help bring together a complex, distributed identity environment, including Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, LDAP/OpenLDAP, SaaS applications, and enterprise platforms, into secure, scalable, automated, and supported identity workflows. The responsibilities include building automation, API-driven integrations, and lifecycle provisioning workflows; serving as a senior technical authority for architecture decisions and escalated engineering issues; driving integration across platforms such as Dayforce, M365, and ServiceNow; providing technical mentorship to other engineers; and collaborating with security, IT, HR, and business stakeholders to translate requirements into engineering deliverables.

We are seeking a well-rounded IAM engineer with strong identity fundamentals, broad integration experience, and the ability to apply those skills across evolving technologies. The successful candidate will have deep expertise in enterprise IAM platforms and protocols and will be comfortable assessing existing identity environments, defining target-state architecture, designing practical integration patterns, building automation, and operationalizing solutions through documentation, monitoring, support processes, and continuous improvement.

What will you do:

• Design, build, and deliver IAM engineering solutions including IGA, IdP/SSO, PAM, and directory services implementations.

• Assess and help rationalize complex identity environments, including distributed Active Directory domains, Entra ID, LDAP/OpenLDAP deployments, application directories, and legacy identity integrations.

• Develop target-state identity architectures and integration patterns that support cohesive joiner-mover-leaver lifecycle processes, secure access, data quality, and operational scalability.

• Configure and support IGA capabilities such as identity profiles, authoritative sources, account correlation, attribute mappings, transforms, lifecycle states, sources/connectors, access profiles, roles, entitlements, access requests, approvals, certifications, and separation-of-duties controls.

• Design, implement, and troubleshoot lifecycle provisioning and deprovisioning workflows across HR systems, directories, SaaS applications, databases, collaboration platforms, and IT service-management tools.

• Develop, test, and deploy identity automation, API-driven integrations, and lifecycle provisioning workflows

• Build and maintain IAM configuration promotion and development workflows, including source control, peer review, testing, release management, and platform-specific tooling such as SailPoint Configuration Hub, SP-Config, SDKs, or equivalent tools.

• Design and maintain RBAC models, including role discovery, role design, entitlement mapping, access-profile design, role lifecycle management, and ongoing troubleshooting of access outcomes.

• Configure and support IdP/SSO integrations using SAML, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), SCIM, and, where needed, WS-Federation and LDAP-based authentication patterns.

• Engineer and support PAM capabilities, including privileged account onboarding, reconciliation, password rotation, verification, decommissioning, safe/vault access controls, approval workflows, least-privilege access, and separation of duties.

• Integrate PAM platforms with Active Directory/LDAP, MFA, ticketing platforms, SIEM tools, cloud services, CI/CD pipelines, and identity governance solutions.

• Automate privileged-account onboarding, reporting, health checks, credential operations, and operational tasks through PowerShell, Python, REST APIs, and related tooling.

• Serve as a hands-on senior technical resource for complex architecture decisions, design reviews, and escalated engineering issues.

• Diagnose and resolve identity-related issues involving aggregation, provisioning, correlation, authentication, SSO, MFA, directory synchronization, access requests, certifications, privileged credential rotation, session access, and connector or platform health.

• Support SLAs, incident response, and root-cause analysis for IAM infrastructure.

• Develop and maintain engineering runbooks, documentation standards, and disaster recovery procedures for identity systems.

• Champion automation-first approaches to reduce manual effort across access provisioning, certification, and onboarding workflows.

• Provide technical guidance, code review, and mentorship to other engineers on the IAM team.

• Partner with security, IT, HR, and business stakeholders to gather requirements and translate them into engineering deliverables.

What you will need to have:

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field.

• Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in IAM engineering.

• Hands-on expertise with enterprise IAM platforms across IGA, IdP/SSO (e.g., Okta, Entra ID), PAM, directory services, lifecycle management, and access governance.

• Strong understanding of IAM fundamentals, including authentication, authorization, RBAC, ABAC concepts, least privilege, separation of duties, access reviews, joiner-mover-leaver processes, identity data management, and privileged access controls.

• Experience implementing or supporting an IGA platform, preferably SailPoint Identity Security Cloud or a comparable enterprise IGA solution.

• Experience with IGA capabilities such as authoritative-source integration, account aggregation, correlation, identity profiles, attribute mappings, provisioning, access requests, approvals, certifications, access profiles, roles, entitlements, and lifecycle workflows.

• Strong knowledge of standards and protocols such as OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML 2.0, and SCIM.

• Experience configuring and troubleshooting SSO, provisioning, MFA, directory synchronization, conditional/adaptive access controls, and application integrations in platforms such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, or equivalent IdPs.

• Experience with a PAM platform, preferably CyberArk or an equivalent enterprise solution, including privileged-account lifecycle management, safe/vault administration, platform and policy configuration, credential rotation, reconciliation, and session management.

• Proven experience building REST API-driven identity integrations and lifecycle automation using Python, PowerShell, Java, or similar languages in orchestration platformes such as Okta Workflows, Gitlab, Jenkins or similar.

• Experience using APIs, scripting, and automation to manage IAM configurations, perform reporting, conduct health checks, and reduce operational overhead.

• Experience with directory services administration and governance, including Active Directory, OpenLDAP, and cloud-based IdPs.

• Solid understanding of identity data management, including attribute normalization, identity matching and correlation, duplicate identity resolution, data-quality remediation and database connectivity concepts (e.g., PostgreSQL, JDBC/ODBC).

• Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, deliver under pressure, and lead complex technical workstreams.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences.

What would be nice to have:
